programme: E2F2 drives S-phase entry and transcription of DNA-replication/checkpoint genes (CDC6, PCNA, MCM5, CCNE1, CHEK1, BRCA1), while KAT5 (TIP60) — acting through its own NuA4 HAT-complex targets (EP400, TRRAP, ACTL6A, H2AZ1) and p53-family checkpoint genes (TP53, TP73, CDKN1A, RRM1) — chromatin-licenses that same checkpoint/DNA-damage-response network. Together E2F2 and KAT5 describe a cell-cycle-checkpoint transcriptional module, not a single physical complex.
role_in_a: In Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma this axis underlies a G2/M-checkpoint-associated molecular subtype built on E2F2 (PMID 38617927) and a histone-acetylation-based ccRCC subtyping scheme built in part on KAT5 (PMID 34631694) — checkpoint/proliferative dysregulation used to stratify tumors and predict immunotherapy response.
role_in_b: In lower_grade_glioma_and_glioblastoma, E2F2 is a direct proliferation driver acting downstream of PPARα/miR-214 signalling (PMID 29862267). KAT5 itself has no disease-specific evidence in this record, so only the E2F2 half of the module is documented for glioma.
shared_axis: Both tumor types are highly proliferative, checkpoint-dysregulated cancers in which E2F-driven replication is coupled to acetylation-based chromatin control of the same checkpoint genes (CDKN1A, TP53, CHEK1); recurrent independent selection of E2F2 (and, in kidney, KAT5) across many patient subgroups is consistent with convergent reliance on this cell-cycle module rather than any kidney/brain-specific interaction.
reasoning: E2F2 is independently documented in both diseases (a G2M-checkpoint gene model in ccRCC, a PPARα–miR-214–E2F2 proliferation axis in glioma) and KAT5 is independently documented in an histone-acetylation ccRCC subtype, so the module is nameable and partly placed by the retrieved record. But no source ties E2F2 and KAT5 to each other or links the two diseases directly through this axis, and KAT5 has zero glioma evidence, so the joint claim rests on general cell-cycle/chromatin biology rather than on anything retrieved. The other ten factors return little or no literature support in either disease and add nothing to this programme.
support: PMID 38617927 — places E2F2 in a G2M-checkpoint-related gene model/subtype in Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma. PMID 29862267 — places E2F2 downstream of PPARα/miR-214 driving glioma cell proliferation. PMID 34631694 — places KAT5 among histone-acetylation regulators used to define Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma molecular subtypes. PMID 28480569 and PMID 28718401 support ATF5 specifically in glioma, but ATF5 has no ccRCC evidence and is not used as a carrying factor here. PMID 41579565 places GATA6 in the ccRCC tumor microenvironment but GATA6 has no glioma evidence and does not belong to this cell-cycle programme.
how_to_falsify: Knock down KAT5 in a patient-derived glioma line and ask whether E2F2-target checkpoint genes (CDC6, CHEK1, MCM5, CDKN1A) lose the acetylation-dependent expression seen when KAT5 is knocked down in a ccRCC line. If glioma checkpoint-gene expression is insensitive to KAT5 loss while ccRCC is sensitive, the proposed shared chromatin-licensing arm does not hold across the two diseases and only the E2F2 arm survives.
caveats: Brain and kidney are anatomically and developmentally unrelated, so any shared axis has to be argued from convergent cancer biology, not shared lineage. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 345 patient-group comparisons, and even the best-supported factor overall (ATF5, 145/345) is concordant in under half of comparisons; the carrying factors used here (E2F2 141/345, KAT5 124/345) are similarly modest, so 'concordant' should be read as 'recurrent,' not as high-penetrance agreement. Two higher-profile candidates were deliberately left out of the story: NFIA and BACH1, which might otherwise suggest a glial-lineage or oxidative-stress/HIF narrative, have no literature placement in either disease in this record. ATF5, the single strongest and best-cited factor overall, is glioma-only and does not extend to ccRCC, so it was kept out of the shared programme rather than forced in. Tissue-generic factors (RFX5, HDAC7, EGR4, FOXP3, STAT4) and single-view factors (ZNF331, PHF5A, ATOH8, SMARCB1, TOX, THAP1, TRIM28, KLF7, ZBTB17, KCNIP3, ATF1, HLF) were already removed before this analysis and play no role in it.
